records.title: Global Blue-Water Naval Order of Battle (Table 3, ca. 2021) & McDevitt's 2035 425-Ship PLA Navy Forecast vs. the U.S. Navy's 355-Ship Goal (CN21-C3, CN21-C8)
records.author_org: Rear Adm. Michael A. McDevitt, USN (Ret.) (2020) / DoD, ONI, IISS, CRS (Ronald O'Rourke), Rick Joe & Bernard Cole (2003)
records.type: Comparative Naval Order of Battle & 15-Year Force-Structure Projection
records.description: Compares blue-water-capable ship inventories ca. 2021 in Table 3 (China 132 vs. US 236+25 LCS, Russia 70, Japan 46, UK 37, India 33, France 26; plus ~175 Chinese near-seas ships = ~270 missile-capable units facing USN 7th Fleet) against Bernard Cole's 2003 baseline (<20 warships, 3 oilers), and projects a 2035 PLAN of ~425 warships: 265 blue-water ships (+150 new minus ~13 retired 2005–10 ships, including 5–6 carriers and ~1.5 SSNs/yr from Huludao) + 160 near-seas ships (replacing ~80 Houbei FACs with ASW corvettes/frigates).
records.use_description: The papers use the author’s period inventory as a baseline and treat forecasts as dated projections.

connection_review.finding: Li’s later conclusion offers a distinct forecast/context. No explicit citation of McDevitt’s 425-ship table was recovered.
Yin He’s replenishment proposal is relevant to future sustainment, not a recovered citation or validation of McDevitt’s fleet forecast.
